subject: Private deployment options — networking & data residency (Acme Medical)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Kline <alice.kline@acme-med.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 13:05:12 -0800
Subject: Private deployment options — networking & data residency (Acme Medical)

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the context on your regulatory constraints and the production use case for the imaging pipeline. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Key pain points you called out
- PHI must remain within Acme's VPC/on-prem environment (no persistent egress of raw data).
- Regulatory drivers: state health data residency + upcoming audit window (Q3).
- Air-gap / limited outbound connectivity for clinical systems — any external access must go through an approved jump host with strict egress controls.
- Need for HSM/KMS integration for key management and audit logging.

Goals we mapped
- Proof-of-concept: Private deployment (VPC peering or on-prem package) that keeps inference within your network boundaries.
- Provide evidence for compliance reviewers: SOC2 artifacts, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration plan.
- Timeline: target pilot by end of Q2 if we can lock networking and procurement.

Technical constraints discussed
- No direct outbound to internet from clinical subnet — we discussed either VPC peering to a dedicated Redwood VPC in your account or our on-prem air-gapped package where we run the inference runtime inside your network.
- Required ports and allowed endpoints will be limited to specific AWS endpoints (if using VPC) or internal jump-host endpoints for the on-prem option.

Immediate next steps / asks from Acme
1) Share a high-level network diagram showing the clinical subnet, any NAT/jump hosts, and where a Redwood VPC or on-prem appliance would sit (we provided a template as an attachment).
2) Confirm list of stakeholders for technical deep-dive: IT Ops, Security, Procurement (we can coordinate a joint call).
3) Clarify whether an HSM/KMS is available in-scope for this project (mechanism and contact).

Attachments: redwood-private-overview.pdf (attached) — high-level options and checklist.

I’m looping Marcus (solutions engineer) and Laura (AE manager) so they’re in the loop for the technical and commercial follow-ups. Once we get the network diagram we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev (our SE) to validate firewall rules and any on-prem requirements.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0172

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: it_ops@acme-med.com, Alice Kline <alice.kline@acme-med.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 14:21:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment options — networking & data residency (Acme Medical)

Hi Jacob / IT Ops team — thanks for jumping in. Quick tech pre-reqs so our SEs can validate feasibility before the deep-dive: 

Questions for your network/security team
- Can you share the high-level network diagram (attach if possible) — include subnets, NAT/jump host, and where the inference cluster would be hosted. We attached a network template that often helps.
- Is there an approved jump host / bastion with outbound egress rules? If so, can you share host access method and whether it supports TLS inspection?
- Are there firewall/NACL controls that block outbound to AWS endpoints? If VPC peering is not possible, would a dedicated private link be acceptable?
- For KMS/HSM: do you have a cloud KMS (AWS KMS) or an on-prem HSM appliance? Contact for your security lead would be helpful.
- Any procurement constraints: contract signatory, PO process, and any required insurance or SLAs we should plan for.

Attachments: network_template.xlsx (blank diagram + checklist).

Once we have the diagram Dev (cc’d) will propose a minimal port list and an implementation checklist. Proposed timing: schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week — please share availability.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: it_ops@acme-med.com, Alice Kline <alice.kline@acme-med.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment options — networking & data residency (Acme Medical)

Hi Jacob / Alice — thanks for the quick responses and for looping IT Ops in. A few clarifying notes from the SE side and suggested next steps: 

Technical notes
- VPC peering is our preferred path for quickest pilot if your security team allows peering to a dedicated Redwood account VPC. That avoids opening general outbound and keeps traffic within AWS backbone.
- If peering is not allowed, our on-prem package supports an air-gapped deployment where the inference runtime runs inside your network and we coordinate offline packaging and installers. That path requires a maintenance window and access to an internal jump host for initial deployment.

Minimal information we need ahead of the deep-dive
1) Network diagram (diagram + CIDR ranges for the clinical subnet and any NAT/jump hosts).
2) Outbound restrictions: list of allowed IPs / FQDNs or confirmation that peering is required.
3) If using HSM: model/vendor and contact. If AWS KMS: whether cross-account grant can be used.
4) Expected throughput (avg RPS and peak concurrency) and desired latency SLO — this drives sizing for Dedicated pool vs. on-prem instance counts.

Proposed next steps
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive next week (Marcus and I will lead). Please propose two 1-hour slots.
- If comfortable, attach the network diagram in reply. We will produce a short implementation checklist and a minimal port list before the call.
- We’ll also prepare SOC2 evidence and a short playbook on data flow for your compliance reviewers (attaching a draft playbook).

Attachment: private_deploy_playbook.pdf (draft — includes data flow diagrams, audit log examples, and KMS integration notes).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0124
